title: Item
description: A made or gathered object a person can hold. Distinct from an `artifact`, which is a named thing canon treats as a character in its own right and which has a power and a cost -- an item is ordinary, repeatable, and describes a category of object rather than one famous one. The Mask of Tethys is an artifact. A reed rope is an item, and there are thousands of them.

base_item.description: Another item this one is a variety of. Inherit, then override -- the shape Factorio's prototypes take, and one canon already uses twice under other names (`fauna.base_species`, `character.reincarnation_of`). A bone harpoon states what makes it a harpoon and lets `item_hafted_tool` say the rest. Cycles are a lint failure; the chain must terminate.

kind.description: Coarse category, for grouping rather than for rules. `weapon` exists as a category because refusing to name the category would not make the spears go away -- what canon lacks is a vocabulary for *damage*, not for the noun. See affordances.json.

affords.description: What this lets a person do, from database/affordances.json. At least one: an object that affords nothing is scenery, and scenery belongs in a point of interest's description rather than in a satchel. Pinned against the vocabulary file by lint in both directions.

materials.description: `material_` ids this is made of. Descriptive rather than a recipe -- it says what the thing is, where a recipe says what it takes to get one. The two can honestly differ: a recipe may allow any `#fibre` where the canonical object is reed.

made_by.description: `culture_`-free by design: this names `character_` or `faction_` ids where canon records a particular maker. Which cultures know a thing is a property of the recipe, not the object.

epochs.description: Epoch ids. Absent means every epoch -- right for a rope, wrong for anything bronze, so date the metal.
